(card-powerlaw_imf)=
## Salpeter / Kroupa piecewise power law

✅ verified · 3 equations · 2 sources · [API: `PowerLawIMF`](../30-api/imf.md#api-imf-powerlawimf)

N-segment piecewise power-law IMF with continuity enforced at the breaks: Salpeter (1955) is the 1-segment classic, Kroupa (2001) the canonical multi-segment form with the observed low-mass turnover. Exact analytic CDF/PPF per segment (expm1-stable through alpha = 1, audit S4).

| Use it for | Not for |
|---|---|
| ✓ literature-standard Salpeter/Kroupa populations and comparisons | ✗ gradient-based IMF inference as the production default — the segment breaks are C^0 kinks; prefer the SMOOTH Maschberger form (house default) |
| ✓ exact segment-wise closed-form sampling (no solver) | ✗ smooth low-mass turnover shapes (use Chabrier or Maschberger) |

### Parameters

| Name | Meaning | Units | Typical range | Code |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `exponents` | per-segment slopes alpha_i (dN/dm proportional to m^-alpha_i); Salpeter 2.35, Kroupa (0.3, 1.3, 2.3) | dimensionless | 0.3–2.7 | `PowerLawIMF(exponents=[...])` |
| `breakpoints` | interior segment breaks (Kroupa: 0.08, 0.5 Msun) | Msun | 0.08–1.0 | `PowerLawIMF(breakpoints=[...])` |
| `m_min` | lower mass limit | Msun | 0.01–1 | `PowerLawIMF(m_min=...)` |
| `m_max` | upper mass limit | Msun | 100–150 | `PowerLawIMF(m_max=...)` |

### Equations

```{math}
:label: card-imf-salpeter
\xi(m) \;=\; \xi_0\,m^{-\alpha},\qquad \alpha = 2.35
```

*Symbols:* $\xi(m)$: IMF in LINEAR mass, dN/dm (the log-mass slope is alpha - 1 = 1.35) [1 / Msun].
*Assumes:* valid for m >~ 1 Msun (no low-mass turnover).
*Derivation:* [theory page](../10-theory/imfs/classic.md#imf-salpeter).

```{math}
:label: card-imf-salpeter-cdf
N(<m) / N \;=\; \frac{m^{1-\alpha} - m_{\min}^{1-\alpha}}{m_{\max}^{1-\alpha} - m_{\min}^{1-\alpha}}
```

*Symbols:* $N$: cumulative count fraction [dimensionless].
*Assumes:* closed-form; inverted analytically for sampling; the alpha = 1 (and mean-mass alpha = 2) removable singularities use the expm1-stable kernels (progenax.numerics, audit S4) — gradients FD-exact AT the singular points.
*Derivation:* [theory page](../10-theory/imfs/classic.md#imf-salpeter-cdf).

```{math}
:label: card-imf-kroupa
\xi(m) \;\propto\; \begin{cases} m^{-\alpha_0}, & 0.01 \le m < 0.08\,M_\odot & (\alpha_0 = 0.3) \\ m^{-\alpha_1}, & 0.08 \le m < 0.50\,M_\odot & (\alpha_1 = 1.3) \\ m^{-\alpha_2}, & 0.50 \le m < 1.00\,M_\odot & (\alpha_2 = 2.3) \\ m^{-\alpha_3}, & 1.00 \le m \le m_{\max} & (\alpha_3 = 2.3) \end{cases}
```

*Symbols:* $\alpha_i$: per-segment slope; continuity coefficients enforced at each break [dimensionless].
*Assumes:* alpha_2 = alpha_3 = 2.3, so the 3-segment merge used by PowerLawIMF.kroupa() is exact.
*Derivation:* [theory page](../10-theory/imfs/classic.md#imf-kroupa).

### Sources

- {cite:t}`Salpeter1955` — the original xi(m) proportional to m^-2.35 (scanned source; slope ledger-verified) *(Eq. 5 + the luminosity-function fit (dN/dlogm slope 1.35 = linear-mass 2.35))*
- {cite:t}`Kroupa2001` — the canonical 4-segment broken power law with alpha = (0.3, 1.3, 2.3, 2.3) *(Eq. 2)*

### Code & validation

- code: [`PowerLawIMF`](https://github.com/jaxstro/progenax/blob/main/src/progenax/imf/power_law.py) (`src/progenax/imf/power_law.py`)
- validation: `tests/validation/test_imf_physics.py::TestSalpeterSlope::test_salpeter_high_mass_slope`
- validation: `tests/validation/test_imf_physics.py::TestKroupaBreakpoints::test_kroupa_segment_slopes`
- validation: `tests/validation/test_imf_physics.py::TestMeanMassAccuracy::test_mean_mass_resolution_converged`


(card-chabrier)=
## Chabrier (2003) lognormal + power law

✅ verified · 1 equation · 2 sources · [API: `ChabrierIMF`](../30-api/imf.md#api-imf-chabrierimf)

Lognormal low-mass body joined continuously to a Salpeter-like power-law tail at 1 Msun — the single-star (disk) IMF of Chabrier (2003). Smoother at low mass than a broken power law. The implemented sampler uses analytic inverse pieces for its initial guess, followed by 30 fixed Newton steps.

| Use it for | Not for |
|---|---|
| ✓ literature-standard Chabrier single-star populations | ✗ a sampler without iterative refinement (the current implementation uses 30 Newton steps; Maschberger uses its analytic inverse directly) |
| ✓ smooth low-mass turnover with the canonical disk parameters | ✗ system (unresolved-binary) IMF studies without switching to the system-form parameters |

### Parameters

| Name | Meaning | Units | Typical range | Code |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `m_c` | peak of the low-mass density per log10 mass (single-star disk value 0.079 Msun); not the peak of dN/dm | Msun | 0.08 (single-star) – 0.22 (system) | `ChabrierIMF(m_c=...)` |
| `sigma` | lognormal width in log10 m (single-star disk 0.69) | dex | 0.55–0.69 | `ChabrierIMF(sigma=...)` |
| `alpha` | high-mass power-law slope (linear-mass convention) | dimensionless | 2.3 | `ChabrierIMF(alpha=...)` |
| `m_trans` | lognormal-to-power-law transition mass | Msun | 1.0 | `ChabrierIMF(m_trans=...)` |

### Equations

```{math}
:label: card-imf-chabrier
\xi(m) \;\propto\; \begin{cases} \dfrac{1}{m\,\ln 10}\,\exp\!\Bigl[-\dfrac{(\log_{10} m - \log_{10} m_c)^2}{2\sigma_{\log m}^2}\Bigr], & m \le 1\,M_\odot \\ m^{-\alpha_3}, & m > 1\,M_\odot \end{cases}
```

*Symbols:* $m_c$: characteristic (peak) mass of the lognormal [Msun]; $\sigma_{\log m}$: lognormal width in dex [dex].
*Assumes:* single-star DISK parameters (not the system IMF); continuity enforced at m_trans.
*Derivation:* [theory page](../10-theory/imfs/classic.md#imf-chabrier).

### Sources

- {cite:t}`Chabrier2003` — the lognormal + power-law single-star (disk) IMF and its parameters *(Table 1 (single-star disk: m_c = 0.079, sigma = 0.69); Eq. 17 form)*
- {cite:t}`Maschberger2013` — independent parameter cross-check: his Eq. 8 restates the Chabrier form with k1 = 0.158, log m_c = log 0.079, sigma = 0.69, tail m^-2.3 *(Eq. 8, p. 1727)*

### Code & validation

- code: [`ChabrierIMF`](https://github.com/jaxstro/progenax/blob/main/src/progenax/imf/chabrier.py) (`src/progenax/imf/chabrier.py`)
- validation: `tests/validation/test_imf_physics.py::TestChabrierParameters::test_chabrier_characteristic_mass`
- validation: `tests/validation/test_imf_physics.py::TestChabrierParameters::test_chabrier_pdf_continuous_at_mtrans`
- validation: `tests/validation/test_imf_physics.py::TestChabrierParameters::test_chabrier_high_mass_slope`


(card-maschberger)=
## Maschberger (2013) L3 — the smooth house default

✅ verified · 2 equations · 1 source · [API: `Maschberger`](../30-api/imf.md#api-imf-maschberger)

The L3 IMF: one smooth analytic form that reproduces the Kroupa/Chabrier shape (Salpeter tail + low-mass turnover) with a CLOSED-FORM quantile function. progenax's production default.

| Use it for | Not for |
|---|---|
| ✓ house preference for a smooth density on positive support away from alpha=1 and beta=1, without interior mass breaks | ✗ matching a literature analysis that is DEFINED on Kroupa/Chabrier segments (use those forms for like-for-like comparisons) |
| ✓ analytic inverse-CDF sampling without Newton iterations; timing depends on the workload |  |
| ✓ IMF-parameter inference within the stated domain, with separate likelihood and convergence checks |  |

### Parameters

| Name | Meaning | Units | Typical range | Code |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `alpha` | high-mass exponent (Salpeter-like tail) | dimensionless | 2.3 (canonical single-star) | `Maschberger(alpha=...)` |
| `beta` | low-mass tapering exponent | dimensionless | 1.4 (single-star; 2.0 system) | `Maschberger(beta=...)` |
| `mu` | scale parameter (sets the turnover; NOT the peak mass itself) | Msun | 0.2 | `Maschberger(mu=...)` |

### Equations

```{math}
:label: card-imf-maschberger
\xi(m) \;\propto\; \biggl(\frac{m}{\mu}\biggr)^{\!-\alpha}\, \biggl[\,1 + \biggl(\frac{m}{\mu}\biggr)^{\!1-\alpha}\,\biggr]^{-\beta}
```

*Symbols:* $\mu$: scale parameter [Msun]; $\alpha$: high-mass exponent [dimensionless]; $\beta$: low-mass tapering exponent [dimensionless].
*Assumes:* alpha != 1, beta != 1 (the L3 parameterization); m >> mu: Salpeter tail; m << mu: turnover.
*Derivation:* [theory page](../10-theory/imfs/classic.md#imf-maschberger).

```{math}
:label: card-imf-maschberger-inverse
m(u) \;=\; \mu\,\biggl[\biggl(\frac{P_{\min} + u\,(P_{\max} - P_{\min})}{C}\biggr)^{\!1/(1-\beta)} - 1\biggr]^{1/(1-\alpha)}
```

*Symbols:* $u$: uniform draw in [0, 1] [dimensionless]; $C$: mu/[(1-beta)(1-alpha)]: converts the primitive P to Maschberger's auxiliary G, making this ALGEBRAICALLY IDENTICAL to his Table-1 quantile [Msun].
*Assumes:* closed-form: no Newton solve, no rejection — fully vmap-compatible and cleanly differentiable.
*Derivation:* [theory page](../10-theory/imfs/classic.md#imf-maschberger-inverse).

### Sources

- {cite:t}`Maschberger2013` — the L3 pdf, auxiliary function G(m), closed-form quantile, and canonical parameters *(Table 1 rows 1-4 (G, CDF, pdf, quantile; alpha = 2.3, beta = 1.4, mu = 0.2), p. 1726 — PDF-verified 2026-07-11)*

### Code & validation

- code: [`Maschberger`](https://github.com/jaxstro/progenax/blob/main/src/progenax/imf/smooth.py) (`src/progenax/imf/smooth.py`)
- validation: `tests/validation/test_imf_physics.py::TestMaschbergerProperties::test_maschberger_peak_mass`
- validation: `tests/validation/test_imf_physics.py::TestMaschbergerProperties::test_maschberger_high_mass_salpeter`
- validation: `tests/validation/test_imf_physics.py::TestMeanMassAccuracy::test_mean_mass_resolution_converged`


(card-tapered_powerlaw)=
## Tapered power law (Parravano+2011 STPL)

✅ verified · 1 equation · 2 sources · [API: `TaperedPowerLaw`](../30-api/imf.md#api-imf-taperedpowerlaw)

Power law with an exponential low-mass taper — the Smoothed Two-Power Law of Parravano, McKee & Hollenbach (2011): power law at both ends, smoothly joined. Smooth like Maschberger but WITHOUT a closed-form inverse (fixed-iteration Newton ppf).

| Use it for | Not for |
|---|---|
| ✓ the PMH11 galactic-disk IMF shape specifically | ✗ the production default (Maschberger has the same smoothness PLUS a closed-form quantile) |
| ✓ smooth turnover with an independently tunable taper sharpness beta |  |

### Parameters

| Name | Meaning | Units | Typical range | Code |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `alpha` | power-law slope (LINEAR-mass convention; PMH11's log-mass Gamma = alpha - 1) | dimensionless | 2.3 | `TaperedPowerLaw(alpha=...)` |
| `m_peak` | taper/turnover mass (PMH11's m_ch) | Msun | 0.3 | `TaperedPowerLaw(m_peak=...)` |
| `beta` | taper sharpness (PMH11's gamma + Gamma exponent) | dimensionless | 2.0 | `TaperedPowerLaw(beta=...)` |

### Equations

```{math}
:label: card-tapered-powerlaw
f(m) \;\propto\; m^{-\alpha}\,\Bigl(1 - e^{-(m/m_{\mathrm{peak}})^{\beta}}\Bigr)
```

*Symbols:* $m_{\mathrm{peak}}$: turnover mass (PMH11 m_ch) [Msun]; $\beta$: taper sharpness [dimensionless].
*Assumes:* linear-mass convention: PMH11 write the log-mass slope Gamma = alpha - 1 and taper exponent gamma + Gamma = beta.

### Sources

- {cite:t}`Parravano2011` — the STPL form psi(m) proportional to m^-Gamma [1 - exp(-(m/m_ch)^(gamma+Gamma))] — PDF-verified 2026-07-11 *(Eq. 1, p. 2 (form historically first proposed by Paresce & De Marchi 2000))*
- {cite:t}`Maschberger2013` — the same form in linear-mass notation, as his comparison Eq. 12 *(Eq. 12, p. 1727)*

### Code & validation

- code: [`TaperedPowerLaw`](https://github.com/jaxstro/progenax/blob/main/src/progenax/imf/smooth.py) (`src/progenax/imf/smooth.py`)
- validation: `tests/unit/imf/test_smooth.py::TestTaperedPowerLaw::test_taper_suppresses_low_mass`
- validation: `tests/unit/imf/test_smooth.py::TestTaperedPowerLaw::test_full_cdf_ppf_roundtrip`

:::{admonition} Deviations from the source
:class: caution
- Exponent convention: the code's alpha is the LINEAR-mass slope; PMH11 Eq. 1 is written in the log-mass convention (their Gamma = alpha - 1, their taper exponent gamma + Gamma = the code's beta). Values are equivalent; symbols differ.
:::


(card-truncated)=
## Truncated IMF (operator)

✅ verified · 1 equation · 1 source · [API: `TruncatedIMF`](../30-api/imf.md#api-imf-truncatedimf)

Wrapper applying hard m_min / m_max cutoffs to any base IMF, with the normalization recomputed on the truncated support. An operator card: the physics lives in the wrapped base IMF.

| Use it for | Not for |
|---|---|
| ✓ cluster-mass-dependent upper limits (m_max(M_cl)) | ✗ changing the SHAPE of the IMF (only the support is modified) |
| ✓ regime studies with forced mass windows |  |

### Parameters

| Name | Meaning | Units | Typical range | Code |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `inner` | any IMF implementing the shared protocol | — | — | `TruncatedIMF(inner=...)` |
| `m_min` | hard lower cutoff | Msun | 0.01–1 | `TruncatedIMF(m_min=...)` |
| `m_max` | hard upper cutoff | Msun | 5–150 | `TruncatedIMF(m_max=...)` |

### Equations

```{math}
:label: card-truncated-renorm
\xi_{\mathrm{trunc}}(m) \;=\; \frac{\xi(m)\,\mathbf{1}[m_{\min} \le m \le m_{\max}]}{\int_{m_{\min}}^{m_{\max}} \xi(m^\prime)\,\mathrm{d}m^\prime}
```

*Symbols:* $\mathbf{1}[\cdot]$: indicator of the truncated support [dimensionless].
*Assumes:* shape inherited from the base IMF; support and normalization replaced.

### Sources

- {cite:t}`Marks2012` — the m_max(M_cl) motivation (Weidner-Kroupa relation) for cluster-dependent truncation *(Section 2 context)*

### Code & validation

- code: [`TruncatedIMF`](https://github.com/jaxstro/progenax/blob/main/src/progenax/imf/truncated.py) (`src/progenax/imf/truncated.py`)
- validation: `tests/unit/imf/test_imf_core.py::TestCDFProperties::test_cdf_at_m_max[TruncatedChabrier]`
- validation: `tests/unit/imf/test_imf_core.py::TestCDFProperties::test_cdf_at_m_min[TruncatedChabrier]`


(card-environment_imf)=
## Environment-dependent IMF (Marks+2012 / Jerabkova+2018)

✅ verified · 17 equations · 4 sources · [API: `BirthEnvironment`](../30-api/imf.md#api-imf-birthenvironment)

The functional alpha_3(environment) relations: the high-mass IMF slope as a function of birth-cloud density and metallicity (the Marks+2012 fundamental-plane relation, erratum-corrected, as restated by Jerabkova+2018). progenax's BirthEnvironment + env_to_imf_params — NOT a galaxy-wide IGIMF integration.

| Use it for | Not for |
|---|---|
| ✓ top-heavy IMFs in dense / metal-poor birth environments (per-cluster alpha_3) | ✗ galaxy-wide IGIMF calculations (out of scope; no IGIMF class exists — audit R7) |
| ✓ environment-dependent population synthesis inputs to the binary engine | ✗ environment-dependent brown-dwarf slope changes (alpha_0 stays fixed) |

### Parameters

| Name | Meaning | Units | Typical range | Code |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `rho_cl` | birth-cloud density; optional constructor override is log10(rho_cl / (1e6 Msun pc^-3)) | Msun / pc^3 | 1e2–1e7 | `BirthEnvironment(log_rho_cl=...)` |
| `Fe_H` | metallicity [Fe/H] | dex | -2 – +0.5 | `BirthEnvironment(metallicity=...)` |
| `log_mecl` | required log10 embedded stellar mass in Msun; density is computed from this and sfe if no override is supplied | dex | mapping input guard [3,8], not an empirical validity certificate | `BirthEnvironment(log_mecl=...)` |
| `sfe` | embedded stellar mass / total birth-cloud mass; mapping does not clip or validate this fraction | dimensionless | default 0.33; wider domains unqualified | `BirthEnvironment(sfe=...)` |

### Equations

```{math}
:label: card-fundamental-fit
\alpha_3(\hat x) = \begin{cases} \frac{19383}{10000} - \frac{509 \hat x}{1250} & \text{for}\: \hat x \geq - \frac{87}{100} \\\frac{23}{10} & \text{otherwise} \end{cases}
```

*Symbols:* $\hat x$: adopted rounded Marks density/metallicity coordinate [dimensionless].
*Assumes:* erratum-corrected threshold -0.87 (Jerabkova 2018 Eq. 6); canonical 2.3 below threshold; retained coefficients give a 0.007436 jump at the default hard threshold; implementation clips alpha_3 to [0.5,2.3]; smooth=True is an opt-in tanh blend, not the default.
*Derivation:* [theory page](../10-theory/imfs/environment.md#fundamental-fit).

```{math}
:label: card-alpha3-marks-eq15
\alpha_3 = - \frac{509 R_\rho}{1250} + \frac{143 [\mathrm{Fe/H}]}{2500} + \frac{19383}{10000}
```

*Symbols:* $[\mathrm{Fe/H}]$: log10 iron/hydrogen abundance relative to solar, in dex [dimensionless]; $R_\rho$: log10(rho_cl / (1e6 Msun pc^-3)) [dimensionless].
*Assumes:* paper transcription of Marks 2012 Eq. 15 in physical variables; kernel instead evaluates the fundamental-fit with rounded rotation (-0.139,0.990); its active branch coefficients are 0.0566008 and -0.403128, not this literal expansion.
*Derivation:* [theory page](../10-theory/imfs/environment.md#alpha3-marks-eq15).

```{math}
:label: card-environment-table3-mcl
\alpha_3(\lambda) = \begin{cases} \frac{107}{50} - \frac{47 \lambda}{50} & \text{for}\: \lambda > \frac{17}{25} \\\frac{23}{10} & \text{otherwise} \end{cases}
```

*Symbols:* $\lambda$: log10(M_cl / (1e6 Msun)) [dimensionless].
*Assumes:* Marks Eq.11 and Table3, printed p.2251; equality takes canonical branch; source expression excludes production output clip [0.5,2.3] and opt-in tanh blend; agent-checked transcription; no wider empirical-domain qualification.
*Derivation:* [theory page](../10-theory/imfs/environment.md#alpha3-lambda).

```{math}
:label: card-environment-table3-mecl
\alpha_3(\lambda) = \begin{cases} \frac{159}{100} - \frac{77 \lambda}{100} & \text{for}\: \lambda > \frac{27}{100} \\\frac{23}{10} & \text{otherwise} \end{cases}
```

*Symbols:* $\lambda$: log10(M_ecl / (1e6 Msun)) [dimensionless].
*Assumes:* Marks Eq.11 and Table3, printed p.2251; equality takes canonical branch; source expression excludes production output clip [0.5,2.3] and opt-in tanh blend; agent-checked transcription; no wider empirical-domain qualification.
*Derivation:* [theory page](../10-theory/imfs/environment.md#alpha3-lambda).

```{math}
:label: card-environment-table3-rho
\alpha_3(\lambda) = \begin{cases} \frac{93}{50} - \frac{43 \lambda}{100} & \text{for}\: \lambda > \frac{19}{200} \\\frac{23}{10} & \text{otherwise} \end{cases}
```

*Symbols:* $\lambda$: log10(rho_cl / (1e6 Msun pc^-3)) [dimensionless].
*Assumes:* Marks Eq.11 and Table3, printed p.2251; equality takes canonical branch; source expression excludes production output clip [0.5,2.3] and opt-in tanh blend; agent-checked transcription; no wider empirical-domain qualification.
*Derivation:* [theory page](../10-theory/imfs/environment.md#alpha3-lambda).

```{math}
:label: card-environment-table3-feh
\alpha_3(\lambda) = \begin{cases} \frac{33 \lambda}{50} + \frac{263}{100} & \text{for}\: \lambda < - \frac{1}{2} \\\frac{23}{10} & \text{otherwise} \end{cases}
```

*Symbols:* $\lambda$: [Fe/H] in dex [dimensionless].
*Assumes:* Marks Eq.11 and Table3, printed p.2251; equality takes canonical branch; source expression excludes production output clip [0.5,2.3] and opt-in tanh blend; agent-checked transcription; no wider empirical-domain qualification.
*Derivation:* [theory page](../10-theory/imfs/environment.md#alpha3-lambda).

```{math}
:label: card-environment-lowmass
\alpha_i = \alpha_{i,c} + \frac{[\mathrm{Fe/H}]}{2}
```

*Symbols:* $[\mathrm{Fe/H}]$: log10 iron/hydrogen abundance relative to solar, in dex [dimensionless]; $\alpha_{i,c}$: canonical low-mass exponent 1.3 (i=1) or 2.3 (i=2) [dimensionless].
*Assumes:* Marks Eq.12, printed p.2252; adopts the approximately 0.5 central estimate; excludes production metallicity clip and slope floors; extrapolation below -0.5 is uncertain.
*Derivation:* [theory page](../10-theory/imfs/environment.md#alpha-low).

```{math}
:label: card-environment-marks-coordinate
\hat x = \frac{99 R_\rho}{100} - \frac{139 [\mathrm{Fe/H}]}{1000}
```

*Symbols:* $[\mathrm{Fe/H}]$: log10 iron/hydrogen abundance relative to solar, in dex [dimensionless]; $R_\rho$: log10(rho_cl / (1e6 Msun pc^-3)) [dimensionless].
*Assumes:* retained rounded (-0.139,0.990) approximation to the 98-degree rotation, distinct from literal Eq.15.
*Derivation:* [theory page](../10-theory/imfs/environment.md#fundamental-x).

```{math}
:label: card-environment-jerabkova-alpha3
\alpha_3(\hat x) = \begin{cases} \frac{23}{10} & \text{for}\: \hat x < - \frac{87}{100} \\\frac{97}{50} - \frac{41 \hat x}{100} & \text{otherwise} \end{cases}
```

*Symbols:* $\hat x$: Jerabkova density/metallicity coordinate; distinct rounding from Marks [dimensionless].
*Assumes:* printed Eq.6, PDF p.6; production clips output to [0.5,2.3]; hard-switch derivative is undefined at the jump; smoothing is opt-in.
*Derivation:* [theory page](../10-theory/imfs/environment.md#cluster-density-conversion).

```{math}
:label: card-environment-jerabkova-coordinate
\hat x = \frac{99 R_\rho}{100} - \frac{7 [\mathrm{Fe/H}]}{50}
```

*Symbols:* $[\mathrm{Fe/H}]$: log10 iron/hydrogen abundance relative to solar, in dex [dimensionless]; $R_\rho$: log10(rho_cl / (1e6 Msun pc^-3)) [dimensionless].
*Assumes:* printed Eq.7, PDF p.6; no intercept in the density coordinate.
*Derivation:* [theory page](../10-theory/imfs/environment.md#cluster-density-conversion).

```{math}
:label: card-environment-jerabkova-printed-density
\rho_{\rm cl}/(M_\odot\,\mathrm{pc}^{-3}) = \frac{3 \mathcal M_{\mathrm{cl}}}{4 \pi \mathcal H^{3}}
```

*Symbols:* $\mathcal M_{\mathrm{cl}}$: M_cl/Msun, total initial birth-cloud mass [dimensionless]; $\mathcal H$: stated three-dimensional half-mass radius r_h/pc [dimensionless].
*Assumes:* literal printed Eq.8, PDF p.6; 4pi denominator; twice the adopted 8pi half-mass cloud density at the same mass/radius; this source expression is not implemented.
*Derivation:* [theory page](../10-theory/imfs/environment.md#cluster-density-conversion).

```{math}
:label: card-environment-jerabkova-printed-mass
\hat x = \frac{3 L_M}{5} - \frac{7 [\mathrm{Fe/H}]}{50} + \frac{283}{100}
```

*Symbols:* $[\mathrm{Fe/H}]$: log10 iron/hydrogen abundance relative to solar, in dex [dimensionless]; $L_M$: log10(M_ecl / (1e6 Msun)) [dimensionless].
*Assumes:* literal printed Eq.9 at stated SFE=0.33; this is not the production mass formula; 4pi instead of 8pi adds 0.99 log10(2) to the derived intercept, not enough to yield 2.83; no proposed correction is adopted.
*Derivation:* [theory page](../10-theory/imfs/environment.md#cluster-density-conversion).

```{math}
:label: card-environment-radius
r_h/\mathrm{pc} = \frac{\mathcal M^{\frac{13}{100}}}{10}
```

*Symbols:* $\mathcal M$: M_ecl/Msun, positive numerical stellar mass [dimensionless].
*Assumes:* nominal central fit, Eq.7 PDF p.10; source prefactor +0.07/-0.04 and exponent +/-0.04 uncertainties are not propagated.
*Derivation:* [theory page](../10-theory/imfs/environment.md#cluster-density-conversion).

```{math}
:label: card-environment-stellar-density
\rho_{\rm ecl}/(M_\odot\,\mathrm{pc}^{-3}) = \frac{3 \mathcal M}{8 \pi \mathcal H^{3}}
```

*Symbols:* $\mathcal M$: M_ecl/Msun [dimensionless]; $\mathcal H$: three-dimensional half-mass radius r_h/pc [dimensionless].
*Assumes:* positive mass and radius; half of the total stellar mass is within r_h; Sect.2.1 PDF p.2.
*Derivation:* [theory page](../10-theory/imfs/environment.md#cluster-density-conversion).

```{math}
:label: card-environment-cloud-density
R_\rho = \frac{61 L_M}{100} - \frac{\log{\left(\varepsilon \right)}}{\log{\left(10 \right)}} - \frac{117}{50} + \frac{\log{\left(\frac{375}{\pi} \right)}}{\log{\left(10 \right)}}
```

*Symbols:* $L_M$: log10(M_ecl / (1e6 Msun)) [dimensionless]; $\varepsilon$: stellar mass / total birth-cloud mass; positive fraction, physically <=1 [dimensionless].
*Assumes:* local substitution of nominal radius law into 8pi half-mass density, then rho_cl=rho_ecl/epsilon; positive SFE required by logarithm; existing API does not validate SFE.
*Derivation:* [theory page](../10-theory/imfs/environment.md#cluster-density-conversion).

```{math}
:label: card-environment-generalized-mass
\hat x = \frac{6039 L_M}{10000} - \frac{7 [\mathrm{Fe/H}]}{50} - \frac{99 \log{\left(\frac{100 \varepsilon}{33} \right)}}{100 \log{\left(10 \right)}} + \frac{2161}{10000}
```

*Symbols:* $[\mathrm{Fe/H}]$: log10 iron/hydrogen abundance relative to solar, in dex [dimensionless]; $L_M$: log10(M_ecl / (1e6 Msun)) [dimensionless]; $\varepsilon$: stellar mass / total birth-cloud mass; positive fraction, physically <=1 [dimensionless].
*Assumes:* retained rounded production mass coordinate, distinct from printed Eq.9; 0.6039=0.99*0.61 exactly; 0.2161 comes from intermediate rounding, not exact nominal substitution; exact substitution gives 0.21618378060413992; the constant gap does not change first derivatives in unguarded interiors.
*Derivation:* [theory page](../10-theory/imfs/environment.md#cluster-density-conversion).

```{math}
:label: card-environment-reference-mass
\hat x = \frac{6039 L_M}{10000} - \frac{7 [\mathrm{Fe/H}]}{50} + \frac{2161}{10000}
```

*Symbols:* $[\mathrm{Fe/H}]$: log10 iron/hydrogen abundance relative to solar, in dex [dimensionless]; $L_M$: log10(M_ecl / (1e6 Msun)) [dimensionless].
*Assumes:* generalized production coordinate at fixed SFE=0.33; mass-only route ignores supplied SFE and density override.
*Derivation:* [theory page](../10-theory/imfs/environment.md#cluster-density-conversion).

(card-schechter)=
## Schechter exponential-cutoff IMF

✅ verified · 1 equation · 1 source · [API: `Schechter`](../30-api/imf.md#api-imf-schechter)

Power law with an exponential high-mass cutoff, f(m) proportional to m^-alpha exp(-m/m_star) — Schechter's (1976) galaxy-luminosity-function form repurposed as an IMF for extreme environments / IGIMF-style truncation studies.

| Use it for | Not for |
|---|---|
| ✓ smooth (C^inf) high-mass suppression with a tunable cutoff scale m_star | ✗ the production default (no closed-form inverse; Newton ppf — use Maschberger) |
| ✓ top-light IMF experiments where a hard m_max is too blunt | ✗ low-mass turnover shapes (no taper below m_star; combine with truncation) |

### Parameters

| Name | Meaning | Units | Typical range | Code |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `alpha` | power-law slope | dimensionless | 2.3 | `Schechter(alpha=...)` |
| `m_star` | exponential cutoff scale | Msun | 10–100 | `Schechter(m_star=...)` |

### Equations

```{math}
:label: card-schechter-imf
f(m) \;\propto\; m^{-\alpha}\, e^{-m/m_\star}
```

*Symbols:* $m_\star$: exponential cutoff mass [Msun].
*Assumes:* fixed-iteration Newton ppf (no closed-form inverse); differentiable and JIT-safe.

### Sources

- {cite:t}`Schechter1976` — the analytic form (introduced for the galaxy luminosity function; DOI verified live) *(Eq. 2 (the Schechter form))*
